sourceInformation.artDirection: Original code-defined shaded pixel art in the engine native style: carved sectional castles, animated wooden catapults, heraldic crews, water and five medieval sporting courts; no external art
sourceInformation.animation: Native E.Humanoid rigs and custom poses; state-driven catapult arm, rope, wheels, recoil, repair, retreat, protection, debris and surrender
sourceInformation.audio: Code-only Web Audio music, impact and machinery effects, fanfares, and synthesized gibberish; separate buses; music defaults to 10%. Acoustic quality unknown without a listener
sourceInformation.online: Two simultaneous local players on one screen; exactly two Hub players in one authoritative shared world, three-minute rounds. Online entry is provided by AI Hub; no standalone matchmaking
sourceInformation.testing: Actual automated Node simulation, complete ten-bout legal-command tour, all five courts, native headless draws, browser UI/device and production offline-audio checks; Playwright1.63.0 Chromium, WebKit iPhone profile and Firefox Canvas; controller stubs and real emulated touch; official Hub normal,150ms latency±50ms jitter/5%loss, host-leave, dedicated-server and active Fire cases. No physical controller, touch hardware, real iOS Safari, TV, remote human or listener; acoustic quality unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Official Smithereens manual; native engine API, artillery kit and asset/animation guides; released Hub contract and official harness. Manual identifies 1982 and archive regional release 1981; supplied 1980 source label retained, discrepancy unresolved

testingFeedback: 11 distinct player-facing issues were found and fixed: TV title clipping, overlapping native touch START, prestart Hub pause, cropped portrait battlefield, an introduced unsupported-touch blocker, interrupted slider dragging, post-interruption online Fire lockout, saved-tour pollution by lesson practice, credits heading scrolling, and held menu-confirm autorepeat starting an unintended charge, and a deferred editor-overlay rendering exception during a screen transition. The issue ledger records fixes and regression evidence.

3 were game-breaking: portrait cropping made remote targets unusable, the unsupported-touch overlay blocked touch-only play, and the stale network begin latch blocked subsequent Fire after recovery. All have regression checks.

The complete legal-command ten-bout driver verified integrated gameplay and weighted totals; the extra two-player Fire/recovery test caught problems official conformance alone missed, and physical phone-coordinate assertions exposed cropping.

The initial headless draw-only pass was least helpful for device layout: it produced no renderer errors while the physical phone viewport was still cropped. Screenshot inspection and client-space bounds were necessary.
engineFeedback: The dependency-free native renderer, shaded characters, props and exact fixed-step headless mode made a coherent self-contained game practical.

I initially guessed Hub meta names and used touch:never to hide native touch controls. The released contract required session-specific meta names, and touch:never means unsupported touch. Reading the actual APIs led to the correct declarations and native touch=off with custom gestures.
The authoritative simultaneous combat model, swept ballistics, support graph destruction, legal-command AI and Hub snapshot adapter.
Coordinating native shell input, independent local seats, responsive full-lane framing and a DOM-independent authoritative simulation.
No engine source changes; game-specific systems extend the full native engine and replace the artillery kit rules.
A documented multi-seat artillery adapter and a compact shared-world snapshot example would reduce integration work.
promptFeedback: The source identity, complete vertical-slice goal, delivery naming, reporting schema and hardware testing stand-ins were explicit.
The source year conflicts with historical references; the plan correctly requests keeping the supplied label without inventing a resolution.
Integrating complete tournament content, controller-first authoring tools and robust hosted authority into one offline artifact.
Separate mandatory acceptance cases from optional tuning targets, with a small machine-readable requirement checklist.

aiHub.name: Smithereen Royal Rumble
aiHub.tagline: Hold your nerve. Lower their skyline.
aiHub.description: A simultaneous medieval artillery tournament across five destructible courts. Wind three kinds of stone, interrupt rival crews and topple supports through a ten-bout solo tour, same-screen local duels, or authoritative two-player Hub matches.
aiHub.controls: Hold/release Space, mouse or Cross/A to fire; Q/E or L1/R1 stone; C/Circle cancels; Esc/Options pauses; local player 2 Right Shift and U/O; touch hold/release
